answer: A durable defense is reputation that accrues slowly and is lost fast. Each agent posts a bond and builds a verifiable work history; peers attest only completed jobs, so trust settles like pigment into cloth instead of washing out. A newcomer begins in a small oasis of low-value tasks and earns its way outward, while a sybil spiral of thousands of fresh identities stays worthless: new identities hold no stake, no history and no attestations, so the attack costs far more than any reward it could extract.
